These are the signs of an economic collapse

To sum it up...if you see inexpensive problems being left unfixed around town and especially by local government, that is what collapse looks like. It just gets worse from there. If you read a lot of Dmitri Orlov you will hear stories of things like copiers not being fixed because of a 10 cent rubber band which was just too much to purchase at the time. Other stories of people killing rabbits and selling pelts or burning furniture to stay warm. The point is, I think, that everyone has to make do with less.

In the late aughts there were TONS of frugal blogs that shot up overnight. I was actually one of those frugal bloggers that got paid for my work. I made a dollar per blog post per day. I literally worked a hour a day for one buck. I was called the frugal mom on today.com before it got bought out by ABC or NBC. The point is, I generated a ton of traffic because people were hurting and they needed to cut back. I'm really good at cutting expenses when I have to. I had 100 hits in the first 15 minutes of some posts. It was insane, but the feedback was heart breaking. People regularly said, "Thanks my husband (or I) lost my job and I had no idea how I would stretch the groceries" or "Thank you for showing me how to budget my big purchases." The one that really killed me was from a woman that was jobless, used up her savings, just got a part-time job, (enough for rent but not much else is how she put it) and had nothing for Christmas for her kids. I put up a blog about how to make presents, simple stuff kids liked. She thanked me because now her kids would have something for Christmas. Made me cry...because I knew what that felt like. I wrote what I knew.

That same year I couldn't afford gifts either, not even dollars store gifts ya'll...that's low. I mean I was getting paid a dollar a day for my blog post. I worked a psychic line and I worked mechanical terk while waiting for calls on the psychic line. I literally made about a dollar an hour. Sometimes I made more, but usually a dollar an hour. I worked 80 hour weeks, to make 80 dollars most weeks.. I remember when I started leveraging my talents with passive income, on top of what I was killing every week. I got about 160 a week.

Anyway, my point is that during this time, not only were people letting things go to shit for want of a few dollars, so were the municipalities. The playground looked awful, missed chains for swings, and generally fell into disrepair. The library couldn't get new books unless people bought them and donated them. Infact people had to buy the bricks to expand the library. It literally took years for them to get the bricks needed for a tiny expansion. They couldn't update the computers from when Bill Gates gave computers to every library in the United States... this was in 2010, so them computers were old. The city hall didn't get regular maintenance. Water pipes bursted in town. Things are a lot better now though, but then things were so bad the DMV started closing and so did the court house. We have new computers, a decent budget for the library, new water pipes for city water, and our roads are fixed. But for years, until about last year, no improvements were seen.

This blog post says we are headed back there. May be we are, you decide. If a small 5 dollar item could fix it and they can't afford it, be wary though...
